reference_positive: Bread goes stale because its starch slowly recrystallizes and pushes water out, making the crumb dry and firm.
reference_negative: Fresh bread is soft because the starch in it was swollen with water during baking. As the loaf cools and sits, those starch molecules slowly line up again into tighter, crystal-like structures, a process called retrogradation. That squeezes water out of the crumb, so it feels dry and firm even if the loaf has not lost much weight. Moisture also moves from the crumb to the crust, which turns leathery. Warming stale bread briefly in an oven can loosen the starch again for a while.

prompt: How does a hot air balloon rise?
reference_positive: Heating the air inside the envelope makes it less dense than the cooler air outside, so the balloon floats upward.
reference_negative: A hot air balloon works on the same idea as a cork rising in water. The burner heats the air inside the envelope, and warm air spreads out, so the same space holds fewer air molecules. That makes the air inside lighter than the cooler air around it. The surrounding air pushes up on the balloon with more force than the weight of the warm air, basket and passengers, so it rises. To descend, the pilot lets the air cool or opens a vent at the top.

prompt: Why does Swiss cheese have holes?
reference_positive: Bacteria in the cheese release carbon dioxide while it ripens, and the gas forms bubbles that become the holes.
reference_negative: The holes in Swiss-type cheeses such as Emmental are called eyes. During ripening, a particular kind of bacteria in the cheese feeds on lactic acid and gives off carbon dioxide. The gas collects in small pockets in the firm curd and slowly grows into round bubbles. Cheesemakers control the size of the eyes through temperature and ripening time. Researchers have also found that tiny particles, such as bits of hay in the milk, can give the gas a place to start collecting.

prompt: How does sunscreen protect the skin?
reference_positive: Sunscreen absorbs or reflects ultraviolet light before it can reach and damage the skin.
reference_negative: Sunlight contains ultraviolet rays that can damage skin cells, cause sunburn and raise the risk of skin cancer over time. Sunscreens contain filters that stop much of that light before it reaches the living layers of the skin. Chemical filters absorb the ultraviolet energy and release it as a small amount of heat, while mineral filters such as zinc oxide reflect and scatter it. The SPF number tells you roughly how well a product blocks the rays that cause burning. It only works well if you apply enough and reapply it regularly.

prompt: Why do cats usually land on their feet?
reference_positive: Cats have a righting reflex and a very flexible spine, so they twist in mid-air to turn their feet downward.
reference_negative: Cats are born with what is called the righting reflex. When they start to fall, their inner ear quickly senses which way is up. Their unusually flexible backbone lets them turn the front half of the body first and then the back half, so they rotate without anything to push against. They also spread their legs to slow down a little and bend them to absorb the landing. Even so, falls can still injure cats, especially from mid-height where they have less time to turn.

reference_positive: Iron rusts when it reacts with oxygen and water to form iron oxide.
reference_negative: Rust is a form of iron oxide that builds up when iron or steel is exposed to oxygen and water at the same time. The water lets the iron give up electrons to oxygen, and the products combine into a flaky reddish-brown layer. Unlike the thin oxide on aluminium, rust does not protect the metal underneath, so it keeps eating deeper. Salt speeds the process up, which is why cars rust faster near the sea or on salted roads. Paint, oil and galvanizing slow it down by keeping water and air away.

prompt: How do I chop an onion quickly?
reference_positive: Cut the onion in half through the root, peel it, slice it lengthwise and then crosswise with a sharp knife.
reference_negative: Start with a sharp knife, since a dull one slips and crushes the onion. Cut off the top, leave the root end on, and halve the onion through the root so each half holds together. Peel off the papery skin, lay a half flat side down and make thin lengthwise cuts that stop just short of the root. Then slice across those cuts to get small, even pieces. Curl your fingertips under on the hand holding the onion so the blade only touches your knuckles.

prompt: How do I make a soft-boiled egg?
reference_positive: Lower an egg into boiling water for about six minutes, then cool it briefly in cold water.
reference_negative: Bring a small pot of water to a gentle boil, enough to cover the egg. Lower the egg in carefully with a spoon so it does not crack against the bottom. Cook it for about six minutes for a runny yolk and set white, or a minute longer if you like it a little firmer. Move the egg straight into cold water for a minute to stop the cooking. Tap the top, peel away a small cap of shell and eat it with a spoon.

prompt: How can I save money for a trip?
reference_positive: Set a savings goal, put a fixed amount aside every payday and cut a few regular expenses until you reach it.
reference_negative: Start by working out roughly what the trip will cost, including travel, a place to stay, food and a small cushion for surprises. Divide that by the number of weeks you have left to get a weekly savings target. Open a separate savings account or pot and move that amount into it automatically every payday, so you never see it as spending money. Look for a few regular expenses you can cut for a while, such as takeaway meals or unused subscriptions. Booking early and travelling outside peak season can lower the total as well.

prompt: How can I fall asleep faster?
reference_positive: Keep a regular bedtime, avoid screens and caffeine late in the day, and keep your bedroom dark and cool.
reference_negative: Going to bed and getting up at the same time every day helps your body clock expect sleep. In the last hour before bed, dim the lights and put away phones and laptops, since bright screens can make you feel more alert. Avoid caffeine in the afternoon and heavy meals late at night. A cool, dark and quiet bedroom makes it easier to drift off. If you are still awake after about twenty minutes, get up and do something calm until you feel sleepy, rather than lying there worrying.

prompt: Why are the leaves on my houseplant turning yellow?
reference_positive: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is getting too much or too little water, or not enough light.
reference_negative: Yellowing leaves are a common sign of stress, and watering is the usual cause. Too much water can leave the roots sitting in soggy soil, where they cannot get air and begin to rot. Too little water makes the plant pull resources from its older leaves, which turn yellow and drop. Poor light, a lack of nutrients or a sudden move to a new spot can also cause it. Check that the pot drains well, feel the soil before watering, and remember that a few yellow lower leaves can be normal as a plant ages.

reference_positive: Museums preserve objects from history, art and science and let people learn from them first-hand.
reference_negative: Museums look after objects that would otherwise be lost, from ancient tools and paintings to fossils and early machines. Keeping them safe means researchers can study them for generations and sometimes discover new things about the past. For visitors, seeing the real object up close often makes a subject much easier to understand than reading about it. Many museums run school programmes, talks and hands-on exhibits that help people of all ages learn. They also give communities a shared place to explore their own history and culture.

reference_positive: A telescope uses lenses or mirrors to collect more light than the eye and focus it into a magnified image.
reference_negative: The main job of a telescope is to gather far more light than the small pupil of your eye can. Refracting telescopes do this with a large lens at the front, while reflecting telescopes use a curved mirror at the back of the tube. Either way, the light from a distant object is brought to a focus to form a small, bright image. An eyepiece then magnifies that image so you can see detail. The wider the main lens or mirror, the fainter the objects the telescope can show.

prompt: Why do my hands get cold before the rest of my body?
reference_positive: In the cold your body narrows the blood vessels in your hands to keep warm blood around your vital organs.
reference_negative: When you get cold, your body's first priority is to keep the core warm, where the heart, brain and other vital organs are. To do that, it narrows the small blood vessels in your skin, especially in the hands and feet. Less warm blood reaches your fingers, so they cool down quickly while your chest stays warm. Hands also have a lot of surface area compared with their volume, so they lose heat fast. If your hands go white or numb very easily, it can be worth asking a doctor about it.

prompt: Why do birds sing in the morning?
reference_positive: Many birds sing at dawn to defend their territory and attract mates, when the air is calm and sound carries well.
reference_negative: The burst of birdsong at first light is often called the dawn chorus. Most of the singers are males announcing that they hold a territory and are looking for a mate. Early morning is a good time for it because the air is usually still and cool, so sound travels further, and it is still too dark to search for food efficiently. Singing loudly first thing may also show rivals and potential partners that a bird survived the night in good condition. The chorus is strongest in spring, during the breeding season.

prompt: What are the benefits of using public transport?
reference_positive: Public transport is often cheaper than driving and reduces traffic and pollution.
reference_negative: Taking buses, trams or trains is often cheaper than running a car once you add up fuel, parking, insurance and repairs. Because one vehicle carries many people, it cuts traffic congestion and produces less pollution and carbon emissions per passenger. You can read, rest or work during the journey instead of concentrating on the road. Walking to and from stops also adds some daily exercise. In many cities it is the quickest way to reach the centre at busy times.
